about: MUTATING — open the public mirror's pull request BY MACHINE: the machine step of publish-to-github v6 (design 7b59af2c, David 2026-09-08: the mirror is 'strictly a backup of source protocol' and the PR 'should open from our dauld GitHub account'). The dispatcher rule publish-github-pr-on-open-pr-ready files this when David signs the protocol's approve step. Runs infra/forge/publish-github-pr.sh with no packet-supplied text — the one arg it admits is the literal `--check`, the verb's own no-network input check (6964f9e8: without it the only way to exercise the verb through the runner was the real run). A run (no arg) finds the one open publish-to-github packet whose open-pr step is ready, fetches forge main from the Forgejo repository on this host (a path, no forge token) and the mirror's main anonymously, builds the dated SNAPSHOT commit (git commit-tree <forge tree> -p <mirror main> — the mirror's history is publish snapshots; a merge conflicts in hundreds of files), pushes it to the dauld fork as publish/<date>-<snapshot>, a branch of its own that is never force-pushed (backlog 1f0aa60d: a second publish on one day force-moved open PR #245's head onto its date-only branch), forking once if the fork is gone, opens the PR against algedonic-dev/boss as dauld, and completes open-pr with pr_url and snapshot_commit. SINCE BACKLOG 02b65d81 (2026-09-27: packet 8d7a3507's approve completed with sign_offs [] and this verb published 660 commits anyway) a ready open-pr is not an approval: before any fetch the run reads the approve step off the record and refuses — naming what failed, nothing fetched or pushed — unless it is completed `approved` with a live presence (passkey) stamp for every required role bound to its CURRENT shape (infra/lib/step-shape.sh, the ops-runner's one copy) and made by an employee this file's `approvers` names (every live stamp too: a named list, never a role), naming source_sha = scanned_sha as 40-hex shas equal to what the measure step recorded, over a clean secrets scan — and the run then scans the approved commit ITSELF, refusing unless that comes back clean, because the measure step's word is an agent's transcription nothing signs; the snapshot then carries EXACTLY that commit's tree, refused when it is no longer on forge main's history, never forge main's newer head. Bounded by construction: fixed repos and branch name, nothing packet-supplied; it never touches the mirror's main — the merge on GitHub stays David's. The dauld token is READ from /etc/boss-publish/github.token (credentials registry id dauld-github-token; provisioned by David's token admin) and never printed; a missing token is a loud refusal naming the path. Idempotent: the snapshot's tree and dates are the approved commit's, so a re-run for the same packet rebuilds the same commit, its push is a no-op, and the PR already open for its branch is found in the open-PR listing and reused. Then closes each OLDER open publish/<date> PR from the same fork as superseded by today's, which contains it (backlog d4bfe548, David 2026-09-24), with a comment naming the new PR, GitHub read back to prove the close, and the older packet annotated — it closes nothing but its own older publish snapshots. Its own timeout: a first push of the whole tree exceeds the runner's 30s default. Authorized by David 2026-09-08 via the design packet, same explicit per-verb process as reclaim-disk / rollback-to / converge / mirror-base-images.
